message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films that have earned a reputation for spooking audiences. Pick whatever fits your mood—whether you’re after psychological dread, supernatural chills, or gore‑heavy thrills.

| # | Title | Year | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|----------|------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | Stanley Kubrick | A masterclass in atmospheric dread; Jack Nicholson’s iconic performance and the film’s unsettling imagery make it a must‑see. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | Ari Aster | A modern psychological horror that blends family drama with supernatural terror; the ending is unforgettable. |
| 3 | **Get Out** | 2017 | Jordan Peele | A sharp social satire wrapped in a thriller; the tension builds from the first scene. |
| 4 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | James Wan | A well‑crafted haunted‑house story that spawned a franchise; the pacing and scares feel fresh. |
| 5 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | John Krasinski | Silence is the main weapon; the film’s premise keeps you on edge throughout. |
| 6 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | Ari Aster | A daylight horror that turns a pastoral festival into a nightmare; the visuals are stunningly unsettling. |
| 7 | **It Follows** | 2014 | David Robert Mitchell | A unique premise—an invisible curse that follows you—creates constant paranoia. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | Jennifer Kent | A psychological horror about grief that turns into a literal monster; the atmosphere is chilling. |
| 9 | **The Ring** | 2002 | Gore Verbinski | A modern retelling of a Japanese horror classic; the cursed videotape trope feels fresh. |
| 10 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | William Friedkin | A landmark in horror; its religious themes and practical effects still terrify viewers. |
| 11 | **Suspiria** (2018) | 2018 | Luca Guadagnino | A reimagining of Dario Argento’s 1977 film; the color palette and choreography are hypnotic. |
| 12 | **The Witch** | 2015 | Robert Eggers | A slow‑burn period horror that uses historical authenticity to build dread. |
| 13 | **Paranormal Activity** | 2007 | Oren Peli | Found‑footage style that makes the supernatural feel immediate and personal. |
| 14 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | Drew Goddard | A meta‑take on horror tropes that delivers both laughs and genuine scares. |
| 15 | **M3GAN** | 2023 | Gerard Johnstone | A contemporary take on the “killer doll” trope; the AI angle feels eerily relevant. |

Feel free to pick a few from different eras or sub‑genres to keep your horror marathon varied. Enjoy the chills!
